quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: The bakery on Elm Street has a hand-written sign on the door: "Back in ten minutes." It has been there since Monday. The lights are off, the chairs are stacked on the tables and a pile of unopened post lies on the mat. A neighbour who used to buy bread there every morning says the owner, who is in his seventies, had talked for months about retiring. The window display still holds a tray of rolls, now as hard as stone. Several regulars have left notes on the door, wishing him well.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the bakery?
options: The owner has probably stopped trading for good
The owner is away on a short holiday this week
The shop is being redecorated before reopening
The bakery has moved to a bigger site nearby
quests.correctAnswer: The owner has probably stopped trading for good
quests.hint: Put the clues together: the sign, the post, the rolls and the neighbour's remark.
quests.explanation: A sign left up for days, unopened post and stale rolls show it has not been open for some time, and the neighbour mentions retirement. "Back in ten minutes" is clearly not true.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Tomas checked the departure board for the third time. The flight to Oslo, which was due to leave at 6:40, now showed a new time of 9:15, and the queue at the customer desk stretched past the coffee shop. He sent a short message to his sister: "Don't leave home yet. I'll text when I know more." Then he bought a sandwich, found a seat near a socket and opened his laptop, deciding that if he was going to wait, he might as well finish the report.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Tomas's sister?
options: She works at the airport as a ground agent
She is on the same flight to Oslo
She plans to pick him up or meet him
She cancelled his flight by mistake
quests.correctAnswer: She plans to pick him up or meet him
quests.hint: Ask why one person would tell another not to leave home.
quests.explanation: Telling her not to leave suggests she was about to come to the airport. The passage never says she is travelling or works there.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Local sales of umbrellas have doubled this month, according to shop owners, and several stores have run out of raincoats. Meteorologists report that rainfall in the region has been well above average since early May, and river levels are rising. The city has placed sandbags near the lower bridge as a precaution. Forecasters expect more showers through the middle of next week, with only a brief dry spell at the weekend, and local radio has been carrying flood warnings every hour. Farmers, meanwhile, are worried about their strawberries, which need dry weather to ripen.
quests.question: What can be inferred about this year's strawberry harvest?
options: It may be smaller or poorer than usual
It will not be affected by the weather
It will be earlier than usual
It will be sold in umbrella shops
quests.correctAnswer: It may be smaller or poorer than usual
quests.hint: Connect what the crop needs with what the weather has been doing.
quests.explanation: Strawberries need dry weather and the season has been very wet, so the harvest may suffer. The text does not state this outcome; you infer it.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Dear Dr. Salim, I am writing about the essay due on Friday. I have completed the research and most of the writing, but since Monday I have been in bed with a high temperature, and a doctor has advised me not to work for at least three days. I have attached a note from the clinic. I would be very grateful if I could hand it in on the following Wednesday, and I will of course accept any penalty you feel is appropriate. Yours sincerely, Mei Lin
quests.question: What does Mei Lin imply about her essay?
options: She wants to change the topic
She has already submitted it
She has not started it
It is nearly finished
quests.correctAnswer: It is nearly finished
quests.hint: Ask how much work remains, based on what she says she has already done.
quests.explanation: Research and most of the writing are complete, so only a little remains. The extension request is caused by illness, not by lack of progress.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Adult bicycle for sale, silver, 21 gears, one careful owner. Bought for commuting but cycled fewer than fifty times, mostly on Sundays. Regularly serviced and stored indoors. A child seat that was fitted last year is not included but can be provided for a small extra sum. Reason for selling: no longer have time. Collection only, Ashford. The frame has no rust, the tyres were replaced in the spring, and the bell and lights are included. The saddle is set fairly high, so it would suit a tall rider. Price $180 or nearest offer.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the seller?
options: Has never serviced the bicycle
Cycles to work every day
Is moving abroad
Probably has a young child
quests.correctAnswer: Probably has a young child
quests.hint: Which detail in the ad reveals something about the seller's family life?
quests.explanation: A child seat fitted last year suggests a young child, and "no longer have time" fits with that. Fewer than fifty rides rules out daily commuting.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: We arrived at seven and were shown to a table at once. By eight we had received our drinks and a basket of bread, and the waiter had apologised twice. The main courses arrived at half past eight, cold on one side, and the manager appeared to offer us dessert on the house. To be fair, the dessert was excellent, and I noticed that most other tables looked equally unhappy. I doubt we will return, though I hope they sort things out. The waiter, to his credit, was polite throughout, and the room itself was pleasant.
quests.question: What does the reviewer suggest about the service that evening?
options: The food was excellent throughout
Only their table had problems
It was slow for most of the diners
The manager refused to help
quests.correctAnswer: It was slow for most of the diners
quests.hint: One observation about other tables changes how you read the whole review.
quests.explanation: Seeing "equally unhappy" tables suggests the delays were general, not personal. The manager did offer dessert, and only the dessert is praised.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Dana, I've borrowed your blue jacket for the interview, and I promise to bring it back on Friday. The fridge is empty again, so I left twenty dollars for milk and bread. Please don't wait up; I'm meeting Tara after work. By the way, I noticed the landlord's letter on the table. It looks serious. Maybe we should talk about it tomorrow? I'll wash the mugs in the sink tomorrow, I promise, and the plant on the windowsill looks thirsty. I hope your presentation went well today. Priya
quests.question: What can be inferred about Priya?
options: She has lost her job and needs the money
She dislikes Dana's jacket and wants it back
She is angry about the empty fridge
She is concerned about the landlord's letter
quests.correctAnswer: She is concerned about the landlord's letter
quests.hint: Look at the tone of the closing lines rather than the practical details.
quests.explanation: Priya calls the letter serious and suggests talking, which shows concern. The jacket is borrowed for an interview, so she does not dislike it.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The town's annual duck race, which has raised money for the children's hospital for twenty years, will not take place this summer. Organisers said that too few volunteers had come forward and that the river is currently too shallow to float the ducks safely. The committee hopes to hold a smaller event in the autumn, though it admits that the loss of this year's income will make it difficult to meet its target. Last year's race attracted over four hundred spectators and more than a thousand ducks were sold, but sponsors, too, have been slow to renew.
quests.question: What can be inferred from the passage?
options: Volunteers were paid for their work last year
The river will flood in the autumn and stop the event
The hospital will probably receive less money this year
The race will be held indoors at the hospital instead
quests.correctAnswer: The hospital will probably receive less money this year
quests.hint: Ask who benefits from the race, then what its cancellation means for them.
quests.explanation: The race raises money for the hospital, and the committee admits a shortfall, so donations will likely fall. The autumn event is only a hope.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: When the researchers fed the birds with seeds from the treated field, the chicks developed more slowly than those fed with ordinary seeds. The difference was small but consistent over three seasons. The team stresses that they have not proven the treatment is harmful, since other factors may be involved, but they have asked the farmer to pause its use while they investigate. The study, published in a respected journal, was carried out on a farm in the north of the country and involved more than two hundred nests.
quests.question: What do the researchers seem to suspect?
options: The chicks are ill from another cause
The farmer has been careless
The treatment may affect chick development
The birds dislike the seeds
quests.correctAnswer: The treatment may affect chick development
quests.hint: Look at what they did, not only what they claim to have proved.
quests.explanation: Asking the farmer to stop, even without proof, shows they suspect harm. They explicitly leave other factors open, so certainty is not claimed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Marisol had rehearsed the speech in the shower, in the car and twice in front of her cat. Yet when she stepped onto the stage and saw hundreds of faces looking up, the words she knew so well seemed to fade. She gripped the edges of the lectern, took a slow breath and looked down at her notes. After a few seconds, her voice came, thin at first, then steadier. When she finished, the applause lasted much longer than she had expected. Her friend, sitting in the third row, was smiling in a way she would remember all week.
quests.question: What does the ending suggest?
options: She was asked to give the speech again
The audience was disappointed and left early
She forgot the whole speech and stopped
The speech was received better than she feared
quests.correctAnswer: The speech was received better than she feared
quests.hint: Judge from the audience's reaction compared with her own expectation.
quests.explanation: Long applause "than she had expected" shows a happier result than she had feared. She recovered after a shaky start.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Following last week's discussion, the finance team will move to the third floor from Monday. The building manager has asked us to remove personal items from desks by Friday afternoon. Movers will take care of computers and files. Please note that the new area has no windows on the north side, so those who prefer natural light may want to ask about the east-facing desks early. Details of the seating plan will be posted tomorrow. Parking spaces on that level are limited, and staff who drive are asked to share cars where possible.
quests.question: What is probably true about the new floor?
options: It is smaller than the old office
It has no windows at all
It has fewer desks than staff
Some desks get more daylight than others
quests.correctAnswer: Some desks get more daylight than others
quests.hint: Ask why anyone would need to "ask early" about some desks.
quests.explanation: Only the north side lacks windows, and east-facing desks are worth requesting, so light varies across the floor. Nothing is said about size.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The village has one shop, one bus a day and a cafe that closes at three. Visitors seeking nightlife or shopping will be disappointed. But early in the morning, when mist settles on the lake and the only sound is a distant church bell, it is hard to imagine a more peaceful place. The owner of the guesthouse laughs when tourists ask what there is to do. "That," she says, "is exactly why people come." There is a small museum about the lake, though it opens only on Sundays, and fishermen sell their catch from a hut by the harbour.
quests.question: What does the guesthouse owner imply?
options: Guests come for the quiet, not for activities
The village plans to build more attractions for visitors
Tourists complain constantly about the lack of activities
Nothing worthwhile exists there to see or enjoy
quests.correctAnswer: Guests come for the quiet, not for activities
quests.hint: Work out what "That" points to, then why that would attract guests.
quests.explanation: "That" refers to the lack of things to do, which she says is the appeal. The peaceful mornings described earlier support this.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Dear Mr. Coleman, I am writing regarding the reference you kindly provided last year. I have now been offered a position at the museum in Cardiff, and they have asked for a fresh one. I appreciate that you must be very busy, so I attach a summary of my recent projects, which may help. The interview is on the twelfth of June, and I have followed the work of your college with great interest since I left. If you feel unable to write again, I completely understand, and I thank you for your past support. Kind regards, Nia Roberts
quests.question: What can be inferred about Nia?
options: She lived in Cardiff last year
She has already received the new reference
She is unsure that Mr. Coleman will agree
She is currently unemployed
quests.correctAnswer: She is unsure that Mr. Coleman will agree
quests.hint: Notice how carefully she softens her request.
quests.explanation: Offering a summary and saying she will understand if he refuses shows some doubt. She has an offer, so she is not unemployed.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Ben: Did you see the forecast? Ana: Yes. Wind up to fifty kilometres an hour on Saturday. Ben: So no boat trip? Ana: Not with Grandpa on board. I'd rather wait a week than risk it. Ben: OK. Shall I ring the hotel? Ana: Yes, ask if they can move our room to next weekend, and check the ferry fee for changing dates. Ben: Shall I tell the others in the group chat? Ana: Wait until we have the new dates, or they will keep asking questions. Ben: Fine. I'll also check the weather for the following Saturday.
quests.question: What is the most likely plan?
options: To leave Grandpa at home
To postpone the trip by a week
To sail anyway on Saturday
To cancel the hotel booking entirely
quests.correctAnswer: To postpone the trip by a week
quests.hint: Combine Ana's preference with the two tasks she gives Ben.
quests.explanation: Ana would rather wait a week, and she asks Ben to move the room and check the ferry change fee. Both tasks fit a postponement.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Since the shopping centre opened on the edge of town, many family-owned shops on the high street have closed. Yet Mr. Ivanov, whose hardware store has been there since 1985, says his sales have risen. His customers, he says, come for advice and for the small items the big stores do not stock. "Nobody at the big store will spend twenty minutes helping you find the right screw," he says. He has also begun to offer repair workshops on Saturday mornings, which have proved surprisingly popular, and several of the shops that closed had been open for more than forty years.
quests.question: Why does Mr. Ivanov think his shop survives?
options: Its prices are lower than those in the big store
It is closer to the town centre than the mall
It offers personal help that big stores do not
It opens later in the evening than other shops
quests.correctAnswer: It offers personal help that big stores do not
quests.hint: Use his own example of the screw to see what he values.
quests.explanation: He contrasts his patient help with the big store's lack of it. Price and opening hours are never mentioned.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Monday. The new job is bigger than I expected. My manager smiled all morning and introduced me to at least twenty people, and I forgot every name. At lunch I sat alone because I did not know where to go, and I noticed how noisy the canteen was. By four o'clock I was so tired I could barely reply to emails. Still, on the way home, someone from my team asked whether I wanted to join them for Friday drinks. I said yes before I could think.
quests.question: How does the writer feel by the end of the entry?
options: Tired but encouraged
Confident and unimpressed
Bored and relaxed
Angry and lonely
quests.correctAnswer: Tired but encouraged
quests.hint: A word of contrast near the end changes the mood of the day.
quests.explanation: The day was overwhelming and lonely, but the invitation and quick "yes" leave a hopeful note. "Still" marks the shift.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The east gallery is temporarily closed while our team installs new lighting. Paintings from this room have been moved to the Long Gallery, where they will be on display until 15 March. Visitors who came especially to see the portraits may wish to check the map, since the Long Gallery is at the far end of the building on the second floor. Please be aware that the lift is under repair. The exhibition has been extended twice because of demand, and staff at the information desk are happy to answer questions.
quests.question: Who is likely to find the changes most difficult?
options: Visitors who cannot manage stairs
People who arrive after 15 March
Visitors interested in lighting
Staff who install lights
quests.correctAnswer: Visitors who cannot manage stairs
quests.hint: Combine the location of the new display with the state of the lift.
quests.explanation: The paintings are now upstairs and the lift is out of order, which is hardest for anyone who cannot use stairs. The notice never says this outright.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The company's profits fell by ten percent this quarter, yet its share price rose. Analysts explain that investors had expected a much larger drop and were reassured by the chief executive's plan to cut costs. Meanwhile, employees have been told that overtime will be limited and recruitment paused until further notice. Its chief executive said the results showed the strategy was working, though she declined to give a forecast for the next quarter. Trading on the day was the busiest for three months, and several analysts raised their targets for the company's shares.
quests.question: What can be inferred about investors' expectations?
options: They had expected profits to rise
They ignored the executive's plan
They had expected worse results
They had expected no change
quests.correctAnswer: They had expected worse results
quests.hint: A rise in price after bad news means the news was better than feared.
quests.explanation: Because the share price rose despite falling profits, the fall must have been smaller than expected. The analysts confirm that a bigger drop was anticipated.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The film critics were divided. One praised the director's bold visuals, calling it the most original movie of the year; another said it was so slow that she checked her watch twice. Audiences, however, have been voting with their tickets: the cinema at the shopping centre has added extra evening screenings each night this week, and the film has now been showing for six weeks. The director, who is in her early thirties, says she never expected such a reaction, and some viewers have travelled from neighbouring towns to see it.
quests.question: What do the extra screenings suggest?
options: The film is popular with viewers
Tickets have become cheaper
The film is very short
The critics all loved it
quests.correctAnswer: The film is popular with viewers
quests.hint: Ask what would make a cinema add showings.
quests.explanation: Cinemas add screenings when many people want to see a film. "Voting with their tickets" means audiences are choosing it.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: Please do not park in the space marked "Reserved: Dr. Alvarez", even for a few minutes. Last week, a delivery van blocked the entrance to the clinic while a patient was arriving by ambulance, and staff spent twenty minutes finding the driver. All vehicles left in reserved spaces will be reported to the council and may be towed at the owner's expense. The clinic provides emergency care every day of the week, and its car park has only six spaces for staff and visitors. Signs are also being placed near the entrance.
quests.question: Why was this notice probably posted?
options: Dr. Alvarez wants a larger space beside the clinic
Someone recently blocked access at a critical moment
Ambulances are no longer allowed to use the entrance
The clinic is about to close for the summer
quests.correctAnswer: Someone recently blocked access at a critical moment
quests.hint: A "last week" event in a notice often explains why the rule exists.
quests.explanation: The van incident shows what happens when the space is misused, which prompted the warning. The doctor's space is not being enlarged.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: In her first year, Yuki knew nobody and ate lunch alone. In her second, she joined the climbing club, and by spring she was helping to organise its weekend trips. This year she has been asked to lead the club, but she is hesitating. "It's not that I don't want to," she told a friend. "I just remember how it felt to be the person nobody talked to, and I want to be sure I can make everyone feel welcome." Her friends say she has changed a great deal, though she still hates having her photograph taken.
quests.question: What does Yuki's hesitation suggest?
options: She is afraid of her friend's reaction
She takes the responsibility seriously
She wants to leave the club before spring
She dislikes climbing and wants to stop
quests.correctAnswer: She takes the responsibility seriously
quests.hint: Read her own explanation for what she is worried about.
quests.explanation: Her concern is making everyone feel welcome, which shows she cares about doing the job well. She explicitly says she does want to lead.

quests.instruction: Read the text and choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Applicants for the position will be shortlisted on the basis of their written statements. Because of the large number expected, candidates who do not hear from us within three weeks should assume they have not been successful. We regret that we cannot provide individual feedback. Interviews will take place in the week beginning 6 October, and travel expenses within the country can be reimbursed. Please do not telephone the office to ask about progress, as this slows the process for everyone. The role is based in our head office and includes a generous training budget.
quests.question: What should a candidate conclude if they hear nothing after three weeks?
options: They must send the statement again
Their travel costs are approved
The interview has been postponed
They have not been selected
quests.correctAnswer: They have not been selected
quests.hint: The notice states what silence means. Find the word for making that conclusion.
quests.explanation: The text tells candidates to assume they were unsuccessful if there is no reply. Travel expenses relate only to interviews.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Nora's grandmother never threw anything away: not string, nor jars, nor birthday cards from 1974. When the family finally cleared the house, they filled two skips, and yet the room that surprised them most was the smallest. On its shelves stood neat rows of notebooks, each labelled with a year, in which she had recorded the weather, the garden and, in a few lines, how she felt each day. Nora took them all home. The house, a narrow terrace, was sold last spring to a young couple who are still finding old buttons under the floorboards.
quests.question: What does the passage suggest about Nora's grandmother?
options: She disliked writing and avoided keeping records
She discarded most things as soon as she had used them
She was more reflective than her clutter suggested
She hated gardening and left the plants untended
quests.correctAnswer: She was more reflective than her clutter suggested
quests.hint: Contrast the mess in most of the house with the smallest room.
quests.explanation: The tidy notebooks record her feelings and her days, which show a thoughtful side. This contrasts with the clutter elsewhere.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Prices in the city's rental market rose again last quarter, but the increase was smaller than in the past two years. Estate agents say the number of new flats coming onto the market has grown, giving tenants more choice, while wage growth remains modest. Some renters have begun negotiating for lower rents, a practice that was rare only twelve months ago. A survey of two thousand tenants by a housing charity found that one in five had asked for a cut in rent this year, compared with fewer than one in twenty last year.
quests.question: What can be inferred about the rental market?
options: Landlords have less power than before
Rents are now falling sharply across the city
Wages are rising quickly for most tenants
Fewer flats are available than a year ago
quests.correctAnswer: Landlords have less power than before
quests.hint: Ask what the change in tenants' behaviour says about who holds the advantage.
quests.explanation: More choice and successful negotiation point to tenants gaining strength. Rents still rose, only more slowly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Dear customer, we noticed you left items in your basket yesterday: a grey coat, a pair of leather gloves and a wool scarf, worth $146 before discount. We have reserved them for the next 24 hours, and we have added a small discount to make it easier to decide. If you have questions about sizing or delivery, our team is happy to help by chat. Please note that stock of the grey coat is very limited, and we cannot guarantee it will be available after tomorrow. Thank you for shopping with us, and we hope to see you again soon.
quests.question: What is the message mainly trying to achieve?
options: To confirm the time of a delivery
To encourage the customer to buy the items
To cancel the order that was placed
To report a security problem with the account
quests.correctAnswer: To encourage the customer to buy the items
quests.hint: Consider why a shop would offer a discount and mention limited stock.
quests.explanation: The reservation, the discount and the warning about limited stock all push the customer to complete the purchase.

quests.instruction: Read the passage efficiently, then answer the question.
quests.passage: During the storm, the ferry was cancelled and the mainland bridge was closed. On the island, however, the community centre became a gathering place. Neighbours brought soup, blankets and board games, and when the power came back on after two days, some of them were reluctant to go home. "We've lived here for fifteen years," one man said, "and I only learned the names of half these people this weekend." A local newspaper ran a photograph of the crowd on its front page, with a headline listing everything that had been shared.
quests.question: What does the man's comment suggest?
options: The storm brought neighbours closer together
He plans to leave the island after the storm
The community centre is unpopular with most neighbours
The island has too many strangers who are not welcome
quests.correctAnswer: The storm brought neighbours closer together
quests.hint: Combine his fifteen years with what he only learned this weekend.
quests.explanation: Meeting neighbours properly after years shows the storm created new connections. The reluctance to go home supports this.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: The trial subjects who slept less than six hours were about twice as likely to catch a cold after being exposed to the virus as those who slept seven or more hours. The scientists say the study cannot prove that lack of sleep causes illness, but the pattern was clear across all age groups. They suggest that sleep might be as important for health as diet and exercise. The volunteers, who came from twelve countries, were followed for four months, and wristbands recorded when they slept and woke.
quests.question: What is implied by the study?
options: Older people sleep less than younger people
Poor sleep may weaken resistance to infection
Diet does not matter for health
The virus cannot be avoided
quests.correctAnswer: Poor sleep may weaken resistance to infection
quests.hint: Note the caution in the middle sentence and what the scientists still suggest.
quests.explanation: The pattern points to a link between short sleep and catching colds, though causation is not proven. "May weaken" reflects that caution.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: The council's decision to close the town swimming pool has been met with anger. It says the building needs repairs costing two million dollars and that use has fallen by a third in five years. Campaigners point out that the figures ignore school groups, which use the pool in the mornings but are not counted as ordinary visitors. A parent at Tuesday's meeting said, "If the numbers are wrong, the decision is wrong." A petition to keep the pool open has already collected four thousand signatures, and a local swimming club plans to hold a protest on Saturday.
quests.question: What is the campaigners' main criticism?
options: The pool is too costly for the council to run
The usage figures may give a misleading picture
The repairs would be quick and cheap to complete
School groups are too noisy for other swimmers
quests.correctAnswer: The usage figures may give a misleading picture
quests.hint: Find what the campaigners say the figures "ignore".
quests.explanation: If school groups are not counted, the fall in use may be overstated. The parent's remark makes the same point about accuracy.

quests.instruction: Read the text and answer the question.
quests.passage: Hamid had always assumed that the long, narrow shop his father ran would be his one day. But when his father's health worsened and Hamid took over, he began to see the accounts. Rent had risen, the old customers were retiring and the business had been losing money for years. He kept the shop open for another six months, telling no one, before finally posting a notice about the closure. His younger sister, who lives abroad, learned of it only when she saw the notice online, and customers came in to say goodbye.
quests.question: What can be inferred about Hamid's feelings?
options: He wanted to keep the profits for himself
He blamed his father for the poor decisions
He was relieved to close the shop at last
He found it hard to accept that the shop had failed
quests.correctAnswer: He found it hard to accept that the shop had failed
quests.hint: Ask why someone would keep bad news secret for six months.
quests.explanation: Delaying the announcement suggests reluctance to face the shop's failure. Nothing says he blamed his father or felt relieved.

quests.instruction: Read the passage, then choose the best answer.
quests.passage: Pilots on short flights sometimes have less than an hour between landing and taking off again, and cleaning crews have even less time. Airlines therefore keep small margins in their timetables, which can lead to delays spreading through a whole day. A mechanical fault in the morning may mean that the same aircraft arrives late at every airport it visits, and a late arrival at the last airport means the flight the next morning starts late too. Some carriers now keep spare aircraft on standby at large hubs to reduce this risk, though that costs a great deal of money.
quests.question: What can be inferred about a delay at 8 a.m.?
options: It will be recovered by noon on the same day
It may cause later flights to be late as well
It affects only the first airport of the route
It is caused by cleaning crews working too slowly
quests.correctAnswer: It may cause later flights to be late as well
quests.hint: Follow one aircraft through the day and see what tight timetables do to a delay.
quests.explanation: With small margins there is little time to recover, so the delay carries on. Cleaning crews are only mentioned as another group with limited time.
